issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who acquires immovable property during a non-collusive partition suit may obtain title and consequential relief to the portion later allotted to the transferor.
material_facts: A partition suit concerning the property was pending when the property owner sold it to the purchaser.
The partition suit was found not to be collusive and resulted in a decree dividing the property between the litigants.
The final decree allotted one portion of the purchased property to the seller and another portion to the other litigant.
The purchaser sought a declaration of title and a consequential permanent injunction.
issues.conclusion: The sale was subject to the partition decree and did not affect the other litigant’s rights. It was effective as to the portion allotted to the seller, so the purchaser was entitled to a declaration of title and consequential injunction over that portion, but not the portion allotted to the other litigant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a transfer during a non-collusive suit in which rights to immovable property are directly and specifically in question is not void or illegal, but is subject to the decree and cannot affect another party’s rights under it. If the transferor’s title is recognized only as to part of the transferred property, the transferee’s title is preserved only as to that part. The Court relied on Jayaram Mudaliar v. Ayyaswami, which explains that Section 52 subjects claims to the authority of the court dealing with the property, and Hardev Singh v. Gurmail Singh, which holds that a pendente lite transfer is not void but binds the purchaser to the outcome of the pending litigation.

predicates.declaratory_title_suit_by_pendente_lite_: A purchaser who acquired property while litigation over it was pending brought a suit seeking a declaration of title and consequential relief.
predicates.noncollusive_partition_suit_pending_at_t: A non-collusive partition suit concerning rights to the property was pending when the transfer occurred.
predicates.transferor_sold_disputed_property_during: A party to the pending suit transferred the disputed property to the purchaser while the suit was pending.
predicates.final_partition_decree_allotted_part_of_: The final decree in the partition suit allotted part of the transferred property to the transferor.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking a declaration acquired property during a non-collusive partition suit and the final decree allotted part of it to the transferor, the purchaser is entitled to title and injunction over the part allotted to the transferor.
